summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's central nervous system lymphoma, was admitted for his 18th cycle of maintenance chemotherapy with intravenous rituximab and high-dose methotrexate. He presented with stable symptoms, including persistent but improved floaters, and denied any new neurological or systemic complaints. He received rituximab followed by high-dose methotrexate with aggressive hydration and urinary alkalinization. Leucovorin rescue was administered as scheduled. His methotrexate level declined appropriately, falling below 0.04 µM by discharge. Liver enzymes, which were mildly elevated, showed improvement. A non-contrast MRI of the brain demonstrated stable FLAIR hyperintensities with no new lesions or abnormal enhancement, indicating no evidence of lymphoma progression. He received a seasonal influenza vaccine during admission. He was discharged home in stable condition with adjusted omeprazole dosing and instructions to monitor for fever, chills, or other concerning symptoms, with follow-up scheduled in two weeks.
